title: Kermit was made from a coat
hook: The first Kermit was cut from an old coat, with half a ping-pong ball for each eye.
peek: In 1955 a young Jim Henson made a puppet from his mother's discarded spring coat and a ping-pong ball sliced in two. That puppet became Kermit, though at first he was not even a frog.
lede: Jim Henson was still a student at the University of Maryland when he began making puppets for a short local TV show in Washington, DC. For one of them he took a turquoise spring coat his mother had thrown out and cut it into a simple hand puppet. A ping-pong ball, cut in half, became the eyes. That puppet was the first Kermit.

bullets.text: Kermit first appeared in 1955 on Sam and Friends, a five-minute puppet show Henson made for WRC-TV in Washington. The show ran for several years and gave Henson his start in television.
The early Kermit was a vague, lizard-like creature rather than a frog. He only became clearly a frog by the end of the 1960s, when his look changed and he gained his familiar pointed collar.

Henson performed and voiced Kermit himself from 1955 until 1990. The role then passed to Steve Whitmire and later to Matt Vogel, so the frog cut from a coat has had only three main performers in about 70 years.
The story goes that Kermit was named after Kermit Scott, a boyhood friend of Henson's in Leland, Mississippi. Others have said the name was simply one Henson liked, so the origin is not settled.
